G1300.def:
δια-τελέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 9:7 (הָיָה), Jérémie 20:7, 18 (כָּלָה), Esther 8:13, 2Ma.5:27 * ;] 
prop. trans., to accomplish; used with ellipse of obj. as intrans. (Bl., § 81, 1), and joined to participles (in Ac, Lc., to adj.; see Bl., § 73, 4) with adverbial sense (= continuously), to continue: Actes 27:33.†

G1301.def:
δια-τηρέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc.; before ἀπό (for מִן), as in Psaumes 12:7 (8) ;] 
to keep carefully: Luc 2:51; before ἐκ, Actes 15:29.†

G1304.def:
δια-τρίβω 
[in LXX Lévitique 14:8 (יָשַׁב), Jérémie 35:7 (גּוּר), Tob.11:8, 12, Jdth.10:2, 2Ma.14:23 * ;] 
to rub hard, rub away, consume; δ. χρόνον, ἡμέρας, to spend time: Actes 14:3, 28 16:12 20:6 25:6, 14. Intransitively with ellipse of object (El., § 81, 1), to spend time, stay: Jean 3:22 11:54, Actes 15:35, Actes 12:19.†

G1305.def:
δια-τροφή, ῆς, ἡ
(διατρέφω, to support, sustain), [in LXX: 1Ma.6:49 * ;] 
food, nourishment: 1 Timothée 6:8.†

G1308.def:
δια-φέρω 
[in LXX for שְׁנָא (שְׁנָא (Daniel 7:1-28 only); 1 Rois 17:39, Esther 3:13, al. ;] 
__1. trans., 
__(a) to carry through: before διά, Marc 11:16; 
__(b) to carry about, spread abroad: pass., Actes 13:49 27:27. 
__2. Intrans., 
__(a) to differ: τὰ διαφέροντα, Romains 2:18, Philippiens 1:10 (R, mg., but see infr.); impers., διαφέρει, it makes a difference, it matters: Galates 2:6; 
__(b) to excel: with genitive Matthieu 6:26 10:31 12:12, Luc 12:7, 24, 1 Corinthiens 15:41, Galates 4:1; τὰ διαφέροντα, Romains 2:18, Philippiens 1:10 (R, txt.; for discussion and reff. see ICC on Ro, Phi, ll. with).†

G1309.def:
δια-φεύγω 
[in LXX: Josué 8:22 (פָּלִיט), Josué 10:28 (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;] 
to flee through, escape: Actes 27:42.†

G1310.def:
δια-φημίζω 
in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= דָּבָר, the matter), Marc 1:45, Matthieu 28:15; with accusative of person(s), to spread abroad one's fame: Matthieu 9:31.†

G1311.def:
δια-φθείρω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi. ;] 
__1. to destroy utterly: Luc 12:33, Apocalypse 11:18; pass., to be destroyed, disabled: Apocalypse 8:9, 2 Corinthiens 4:16. 
__2. In moral sense, to corrupt, deprave: τ. γῆν, Apocalypse 11:18; pass., διεφθαρμένοι τ. νοῦν, 1 Timothée 6:5.†

G1312.def:
δια-φθορὰ, -ᾶς, ἡ
(διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת, and cogn. forms ;] 
__1. destruction. 
__2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, Actes 2:27 (LXX), Actes 2:31 13:34-37.†

G1313.def:
διά-φορος, -ον
(διαφέρω), [in LXX for שְׁנָא (Daniel 7:7, 19); also as in Polyb., iv, 188, al., Τὸ δ., τὰ δ., money: Sir.27:1 42:5, 2Ma.3:6 ;] 
__1. different: Romains 12:6, Hébreux 9:10. 
__2. excellent: compar., -ώτερος, Hébreux 1:4 8:6.†

G1314.def:
δια-φυλάσσω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַר (as Psaumes 91:11) ;] 
to guard carefully (M, Pr., 116), defend: with accusative, Luc 4:10 (LXX).†

G1315.def:
δια-χειρίζω
(χείρ), 
to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid. 
__(a) = act.; 
__(b) in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: with accusative, Actes 5:30 26:21.†

G1316.def:
δια-χωρίζω 
[in LXX: Genèse 1:4 ff (בָּדַל hi.), Genèse 13:9 ff. (פָּרַד ni.), etc. ;] 
to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: before ἀπό Luc 9:33.†

G1317.def:
διδακτικός, -ή, -όν
(= cl. διδασκαλικός) 
apt at teaching: 1 Timothée 3:2, 2 Timothée 2:24.†

G1319.def:
διδασκαλία, -ας, ἡ
(διδάσκω), [in LXX: Proverbes 2:17 (אַלּוּף), Ésaïe 29:13 (לָמַד), Sir.24:33 39:8 * ;] 
teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most frequently the latter: Romains 12:7 15:4, Éphésiens 4:14, 1 Timothée 4:6, 13, 16 5:17 6:1, 3, 2 Timothée 3:10 3:16, Tite 2:7, 10; ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., 1 Timothée 1:10, 2 Timothée 4:3, Tite 1:9 2:1; pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Colossiens 2:22; δ. δαιμονίων, 1 Timothée 4:1, δ. διδάσκειν, Matthieu 15:9, Marc 7:7" (LXX) (Cremer, 182).†
SYN.: διδαχή

G1320.def:
διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ
(διδάσκω), [in LXX: Esther 6:1, 2Ma.1:10 * ;] 
given as rendering of Heb. רַבִּי ,רַבּוֺן (NT, Ῥαββεί, Ῥαββουνεί which see); 
a teacher: Jean 1:39 20:16; of Jewish teachers, Luc 2:46, Jean 3:10, cf. Romains 2:20-21; of John Baptist, Luc 3:12; of Jesus, Jean 3:2, 10 8:4 11:28 13:13-14, and often in Syn., most frequently in voc., as title of address, as Matthieu 8:19, Marc 4:38; of Jesus by himself, Matthieu 23:8; of an apostle, 1 Timothée 2:7, 2 Timothée 1:11; of Christians, 1 Corinthiens 12:28-29, Éphésiens 4:11, Actes 13:1, Jacques 3:1; of false teachers, 2 Timothée 4:3 (Cremer, 181; DB, i, 609, iii, 294, iv, 691) 
SYN.: παιδευτής, q.v

G1321.def:
διδάσκω 
[in LXX chiefly for למד pl., also for ידע hi., ירה hi., etc. ;] 
to teach (i.e. instruct) a person, teach a thing; 
__1. trans.: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 5:2, Marc 1:22, al.; before ὅτι, Marc 8:31; περί, 1 Jean 2:27; with inf., Luc 11:1; with accusative of thing(s), Marc 6:30 12:14; with cogn. accusative, Matthieu 15:9 (LXX); with dupl. accusative, Marc 4:2, Jean 14:26; pass., Galates 1:12, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:15; with dative of person(s) (like Heb., cf. Job 21:23, but prob. a vernac. usage, see Swete, in l.), Apocalypse 2:14. 
__2. Absol., to teach, give instruction: Matthieu 4:23, Marc 1:21, and often in Gosp., Romains 12:7, 1 Corinthiens 4:17, 1 Timothée 2:12, al. 
SYN.: παιδεύω (cf. Westc., Heb., 402; Cremer, 180).

G1322.def:
διδαχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(διδάσκω), [in LXX: Psaumes 60:1-12 title. (לָמַד pi.); Sm.: Deutéronome 33:8 * ;] 
__1. objectively, teaching, doctrine, that which is taught: Marc 1:27, Jean 7:16, Actes 17:19, Romains 6:7 16:17, 2Jn.10, Apocalypse 2:24; with genitive poss., Matthieu 7:28 16:12 22:33, Marc 1:22 11:18, Luc 4:32, Jean 18:19, Actes 5:28, Apocalypse 2:14-15; ἡ δ., of Christ, Jean 7:17, Actes 13:12, 2Jn.9; of. τὴν δ., Tite 1:9; with genitive obj., βαπτισμῶν δ., Hébreux 6:2; pl., Hébreux 13:9. 
__2. Actively, teaching: Actes 2:42, 2 Timothée 4:2; ἐν τ. δ., in the course of his teaching: Marc 4:2 12:38; λαλεῖν ἐν δ., 1 Corinthiens 14:6; ἔχειν δ., 1 Corinthiens 14:26 (DCG, i, 485; Cremer, 181).†
SYN.: διδασκαλία

G1323.def:
δίδραχμος, -ον
(δίς, δραχμή), 
worth two drachmae; τὸ δ. (sc. νόμισμα, coin), 
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶל (Genèse 23:15, a1.), also for כֶּסֶף: Genèse 20:16, Deutéronome 22:29 ;] 
a double drachma, nearly equal to the Jewish half-shekel, the amount of the Temple tax: Matthieu 17:24 (DB, iii, 428).†

G1324.def:
Δίδυμος, -ου, ὁ
(prop. name from δίδυμος, -η, -ον, double, sc. παῖς, twin) 
Didymus, surname of the apostle Thomas: Jean 11:16 20:24 21:2.†

G1325.def:
δίδωμι, 
[in LXX chiefly for נָתַן (53 words in all) ;] 
to give—in various senses, accusative to context—bestow, grant, supply, deliver, commit, yield: absol., Actes 20:35; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Matthieu 4:9 5:31, Jean 1:12, al. mult.; with dative of person(s), before ἐκ, Matthieu 25:8; id. with genitive part.. Apocalypse 2:17; with accusative of person(s), Jean 3:16, Apocalypse 20:13, al.; δεξιάς, Galates 2:9; φίλημα, Luc 7:45; γνῶσιν, Luc 1:77; κρίσιν, Jean 5:22; of seed yielding fruit, Marc 4:7, 8; ἐργασίαν (Deiss., LAE, 117f.), Luc 12:58; with inf. fin., Matthieu 27:34, Marc 5:43, Luc 8:55, Jean 6:52, al.; with dative of person(s) and inf., Luc 1:74, al.; with accusative and inf., Actes 2:27, Apocalypse 3:9; with dupl. accusative, Matthieu 20:28, Marc 10:45, Éphésiens 1:22 4:11, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:9, 1 Timothée 2:6, al.; ἑαυτὸν δ. εἰς (Polyb., al.), Actes 19:31; with dative of person(s), before κατά (MM, Exp., xi), Apocalypse 2:28 (LXX); δ. ἵνα, Apocalypse 3:9; δέδωκα ἐνώπιόν σου θύραν ἀνεῳγμένην, Apocalypse 3:8.
SYN.: δωρέομαι.

G1326.def:
δι-εγείρω 
[in LXX: Jdth.1:4, Esther 1:1, 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 15:10, 3Ma.5:15 * ;] 
to arouse completely, arouse as from rest or sleep: Luc 8:24; pass., Marc 4:39, Luc 8:24; of the sea, Jean 6:18. Metaphorical, of the mind: ἐν ὑπομνήσει, 2 Pierre 1:13 3:1.†

G1327.def:
δι-έ-οδος, -ου, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹצָאָה, as Nombres 34:4ff, and frequently in Jos;] 
in π. of the conclusion of a trial (MM, Exp., xi); a way out through, an outlet; pl., δ. τῶν ὁδῶν, RV, the partings of the highways: Matthieu 22:9.†

G1331.def:
δι-ερωτάω, -ῶ 
to find by inquiry: with accusative, Actes 10:17.†

G1332.def:
διετής, -ές
(δίς, ἔτος), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:3 * ;] 
__1. lasting two years. 
__2. two years old: ἀπὸ δ. (sc. παιδός, or neuter; cf. 1 Chroniques 27:23, ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς), Matthieu 2:16.†

G1333.def:
διετία, -ας, ἡ
(διετής), [in LXX (Græc. Ven.): Genèse 41:1 45:5 * ;] 
the space of two years: Actes 24:27 28:30.†

G1334.def:
δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi. ;] 
to set out in detail, recount, describe: absol., Hébreux 11:32; with accusative of thing(s), Actes 8:33; with dative of person(s), before πῶς, Marc 5:16, Actes 9:27 12:17; ἅ εἶδον, Marc 9:9; ὅσα ἐποίησε, -αν, Luc 8:39 9:10.†

G1335.def:
δι-ήγησις, -εως, ἡ
(διηγέομαι), [in LXX: Juges 7:15 מִסְפָּר Habacuc 2:6 חִידָה), frequently in (Sir.6:35, al.), 2Ma.2:32 2Mac 6:17 ;] 
a narrative: Luc 1:1 (cf. Milligan, NTD, 130).†

G1336.def:
δι-ηνεκής, -ές
(διήνεγκα, aorist of διαφέρω) [in Sm.: Psaumes 48:15, 89:30 ;] 
unbroken, continuous: adverbially, εἰς τὸ δ., continually (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 251), Hébreux 7:3 10:1, 12 10:14†

G1337.def:
διθάλασσος, -ον
(δις, θύλασσα); 
__1. divided into two seas (as the Euxine, Strab., ii, 522). 
__2. dividing the sea: τόπον δ., a tongue of land, or reef, running out into the sea: Actes 27:41.†

G1338.def:
δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι, 
[in LXX for בָּרַח hi., Exode 26:28 * ;] 
to go through, penetrate: Hébreux 4:12.†

G1339.def:
δι-ίσπημι
(Rec. διΐσ), [in LXX: Eze.5:1 (חָלַק pi.), Proverbes 17:9 (פָּרַד hi.), etc. ;] 
to set apart, separate; of time (or space), to make an interval, intervene: διαστάσης ὥρας μιᾶς, Luc 22:59; βραχὺ διαστήσαντες, Actes 27:28. In pass., mid. and 2 aor., pf. and plpf. act., to part, withdraw: Luc 24:51.†

G1341.def:
δικαιοκρισία, -ας, ἡ 
righteous judgment: Romains 2:5 (cf. τ. δικαίας κρίσεως, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:5; τὴν δ. κ., Jean 7:24. For use in π., see Deiss., LAE, 89 f.).†

G1342.def:
δίκαιος, -α, -ον
(δίκη), [in LXX chiefly for צַדִּיק (for rendering of צַדִּיק in sense of correct, see Deiss., BS, 115 f.); sometimes for נָקִי as Proverbes 1:11, al. ;] 
in early Gk. writers 
__(a) of persons, observant of δίκη, custom, rule, right, righteous in performing duties to gods and men ; 
__(b) of things, righteous, in accordance with right. 
In NT 
__1. righteous, chiefly in the broad sense, as above, of the person or thing corresponding to the Divine standard of right 
__(a) of persons: of God, Romains 3:26, 1 Jean 2:29 Jn 3:7; of Christ, Actes 3:14 7:52 22:14, 1 Pierre 3:18, 1 Jean 2:1; of men, Matthieu 1:19 (Abbott, Essays, 75 f.) Matthieu 10:41 13:17, 43 13:49, Luc 1:6, 17, Romains 5:7, 1 Timothée 1:9, Jacques 5:6, 1 Pierre 3:12, 1 Jean 3:7, Apocalypse 22:11, al.; δ. καὶ εὐλαβής, Luc 2:25; ἅγιος, Marc 6:20; ἀγαθός, Luc 23:50; φοβούμενος τ. θεόν, Actes 10:22; opposite to ἀμαρτωλοὶ καὶ ἀσεβεῖς, 1 Pierre 4:18; ἄδικοι, Matthieu 5:45, Actes 24:15; δ. ἐκ πίστεως, Romains 1:17, Galates 3:11, Hébreux 10:38" (LXX) ; δ. παρὰ τ. θεῷ, Romains 2:13 
__(b) of things: ἔργα δ., opposite to πονηρὰ, 1 Jean 3:12; ἐντολή, Romains 7:12; metaphorically, αἷμα, Matthieu 23:35; τὸ δ., Luc 12:57; δ. ἐστιν, Actes 4:19, Éphésiens 6:1, Philippiens 1:7; ὅ, Matthieu 20:4; ὅσα, Philippiens 4:8 
__2. In narrower sense 
__(a) of persons, as in later cl. writers, just, rendering to each his due: Tite 1:8, 1 Jean 1:9; δ. κριτής, 2 Timothée 4:8 
__(b) of things: τὸ δ., Colossiens 4:1; δ., sc. ἐστιν, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:6; κρίσις δ., Jean 5:30; ὁδοί, Apocalypse 15:3 
SYN.: ἀγαθός (which see), καλός, χρηστός (Cremer, 183, 690).

G1343.def:
δικαιοσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(δίκαιος), [in LXX chiefly for צֶדֶק, and cognates, Genèse 15:6, al., rarely for חֶסֶד, Genèse 19:19 ;] 
the character of ὁ δίκαιος (which see) 
__1. in broad sense, righteousness, conformity to the Divine will in purpose, thought and action: Matthieu 5:6, Jean 16:8, Actes 13:10, Romains 4:3; λόγος δικαιοσύνης, teaching of r., Hébreux 5:13; βασιλεὺς δ. (cf. FlJ, BJ, vi, 10, β. δίκαιος), Hébreux 7:2; ὅπλα δ., Romains 6:13; ὁδὸς δ., Matthieu 21:32; θώραξ τῆς δ., Éphésiens 6:14; διὰκονοι δ., 2 Corinthiens 11:15; ὁσιότης καὶ δ., Luc 1:75, cf. Éphésiens 4:24; ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δ., Éphésiens 5:9; δ. κ. εἰρήνη κ. χαρά, Romains 14:17; δ. κ. ἁγιασμός, 1 Corinthiens 1:30; opposite to ἁμαρτία, Romains 8:10; ἀνομία, 2 Corinthiens 6:14; άδικία, Romains 3:5; ποιεῖν τὴν δ., 1 Jean 2:29 Jn 3:7; id. as an inclusive term for the active duties of the religious life (ICC, in l; Abbott, Essays, 73 ff), Matthieu 6:1; ἐργάζεσθαι δ., Actes 10:35; διώκειν δ., 1 Timothée 6:11; πληροῦν πᾶσαν δ., Matthieu 3:15; ζῆν τῇ δ., 1 Pierre 2:24; δ. θεοῦ, a righteousness divine in its character and origin, Matthieu 6:33, Jacques 1:20, (where it also includes the idea of God's personal r.; see ICC, on Romains 1:17) Romains 1:17 3:5, 21-26 10:3, 2 Corinthiens 5:21, Philippiens 3:9; ἡ δ. τ. πίσιεως, Romains 4:11; ἡ ἐκ π. δ., Romains 9:30; ἡ κατὰ π. δ., Hébreux 11:7; opposite to this is ἡ ἐκ νόμου δ., Romains 10:5; ἡ δ. ἐν ν., Philippiens 3:6; ἡ ἰδία δ., Romains 10:3, cf. Philippiens 3:9 
__2. In narrower sense (cf. δίκαιος), justice: Actes 17:31, 2 Pierre 1:1, Apocalypse 19:11 (DCG, ii, 529 ff.; Cremer, 190, 690).

G1345.def:
δικαίωμα, -τος, τ
(δικαιόω), [in LXX most frequently for חֹק, in Ez, chiefly for מִשְׁפָּט, in Pss, τὰ δ., frequently for פִּקּוּד ;] 
a concrete expression of righteousness, the expression and result of the act of δικαίωσις, "a declaration that a thing is δίκαιον, or that a person is δίκαιος," hence, 
__(a) an ordinance: δ. τ. θεοῦ, Romains 1:32; τ. κυρίου, Luc 1:6; τ. νόμου, Romains 2:26 8:4; λατρείας, Hébreux 9:1; σαρκός, Hébreux 9:10; 
__(b) a sentence: of acquittal, Romains 5:16 (also Romains 5:18; ICC, in l), or of condemnation; 
__(with) a righteous act: Romains 5:18 (RV), Apocalypse 15:4 19:8 (on the usage of π., see MM, Exp., iii, xi).
†

G1346.def:
δικαίως 
adv. (δίκαιος, which see), [in LXX for צֶדֶק, etc. ;] 
__1. righteously: 1 Corinthiens 15:34, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:10, Tite 2:12. 
__2. justly: Luc 23:41, 1 Pierre 2:23.†

G1347.def:
δικαίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(δικαιόω), [in LXX for מִשְׁפָּט, Lévitique 24:22 * ;] 
the act of pronouncing righteous, justification, acquittal: Romains 4:25 5:18 (Cremer, 199).†

G1348.def:
δικαστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(δικάζω), [in LXX for שָׁפַט ;] 
a judge: Actes 7:27, 35" (LXX) .†
SYN.: κριτής, WH. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer (LS, see word; Enc. Brit. 11, xii, 504 f.)

G1349.def:
δίκη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for נָקָם, רִיב, etc. ;] 
__1. custom. 
__2. right. 
__3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:9; δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7. 
__4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: Actes 28:4.†

G1350.def:
δίκτυον, -ον, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for רֶשֶׁת, שְׂבָכָה ;] 
general term for a net: Matthieu 4:20-21, Marc 1:18-19, Luc 5:2, 4-6, Jean 21:6, 8 21:11 †
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), σαγήνη.

G1351.def:
διλογος, -ον
(δίς, λέγω), 
__1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition. 
__2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Proverbes 11:13, Sir.5:9) double-tongued: 1 Timothée 3:8.†

G1352.def:
διό 
conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ, 
wherefore, on which account: Matthieu 27:8, Luc 7:7, Actes 15:19, Romains 1:24, al.; δ. καί, Luc 1:35, Actes 10:29 24:26, Romains 4:22 15:22, 2 Corinthiens 1:20 4:13 5:9, Philippiens 2:9, Hébreux 11:12 13:12 (see Ellic. on Galates 4:31).

G1353.def:
δι-οδεύω, 
[in LXX chiefly for עבר ;] 
__1. to travel through: with accusative, Actes 17:1 
__2. to travel along (Bar.4:2, 1Ma.12:32-33): Luc 8:1.†

G1354.def:
Διονύσιος, -ου, ὁ 
Dionysius, an Athenian: Actes 17:34.†

G1355.def:
διό-περ conjunct. (διό, which see, strengthened by πέρ), 
[in LXX: Jdth.8:17; Jdt.8.1-36; 2Ma.5:1-27 * ;] 
for which very reason: 1 Corinthiens 8:13 10:14.†

G1356.def:
διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές 
(δῖος, πίπτω, see Page on Ac, l.with; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.), 
fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), Actes 19:35.†

G1357.def:
διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), 
__1. a making straight. 
__2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Hébreux 9:10 (Cremer, 807).†
διόρθωμα, -τος, τό
(διορθόω, to make straight, set right), 
a correction, reform: Actes 24:3.†
διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), 
__1. a making straight. 
__2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Hébreux 9:10 (Cremer, 807).†

G1358.def:
δι-ορύσσω 
[in LXX: Job 24:16, Exode 12:5, 7 12:12, (חָתַר) * ;] 
to dig through: with accusative, of house-breaking (as in π.; MM, Exp., xi), Matthieu 24:43, Luc 12:39; absol., Matthieu 6:19-20.†

G1359.def:
Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ
(Ion. and κοινή form of Att..., Διόσκοροι; Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son), 
the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): Actes 28:11.†

G1360.def:
δι-ότι , conjunct., for διὰ τοῦτο, ὅτι (Lat. propterea quod), 
because: Luc 1:13 2:7 21:28, Actes 13:35 18:10 20:26 22:18, Romains 1:19, 21 3:20 8:7, 21, 1 Corinthiens 15:9, Philippiens 2:26, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:8, 18 (Lft., Notes, 37) 1 Thessaloniciens 4:6, Hébreux 11:5, 23, Jacques 4:3, 1 Pierre 1:16 1:24 2:6. It is usually stronger than ὅτι, but sometimes, as in Luc 1:13, Romains 1:19, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:18, approximates to MGr. sense, for; cf. Milligan, Th., l.with†

G1361.def:
Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες 
(Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus), 
as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jn 9.†

G1362.def:
διπλόος
(poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) [in LXX for כָּפַל, מִשְׁנֶה, and cognates ;] 
twofold, double: 1 Timothée 5:17, Apocalypse 18:6; διπλότιρον, in twofold measure: Matthieu 23:15.†

G1363.def:
διπλόω, -ῶ
(δυτλόος), 
to double: δ. τὰ διπλᾶ, Apocalypse 18:6.†

G1364.def:
δίς 
adv., 
twice: Marc 14:30, 72; δ. τ. σαββάτου, Luc 18:12; καὶ ἅπαξ κ. δ., Philippiens 4:16, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:18; δ. ἀποθανόντα, Ju 12 (see Mayor, ICC, in l); δ. μυριάδες, Apocalypse 9:16.†

G1365.def:
διστάζω
(δίς), 
to doubt, hesitate: Matthieu 14:31 28:17.†
SYN.: ἀπορέω, διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491)

G1366.def:
δίστομος, -ον
(δίς, στόμα), [in LXX: Juges 3:16, Psaumes 149:6, Proverbes 5:4 (פֶּה), Sir.21:3 * ;] 
__1. of rivers and roads, double-mouthed, double branching. 
__2. Of swords (Eur.; LXX, ll with), two-edged: Hébreux 4:12, Apocalypse 1:16 2:12.†

G1367.def: two thousand , (Herdotus Historicus):—;singular with collective nouns, δισχιλίη ἵππος 2000 horse, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G1368.def:
δι-υλίζω
(δια, ὑλίζω, to strain) [in LXX: Amos 6:6 * ;] 
__1. to strain thoroughly (Archytas; Am., l.with). 
__2. Later, to strain out: figuratively, Matthieu 23:24.†

G1369.def:
διχάζω
(δίχα, apart), [in Aq.: Lévitique 1:17, Deutéronome 14:6 * ;] 
to cut apart, divide in two; metaphorically, to set at variance: Matthieu 10:35.†

G1370.def:
διχοστασία, -ας, ἡ
(διχοστατέω, to stand apart), [in LXX: 1Ma.3:29 * ;] 
standing apart, dissension: Romains 16:17, Galates 5:20.†

G1371.def:
διχοτομέω, -ῶ
(διχοτόμος, δίχα, τέμνω), [in LXX: Exode 29:17 (נָתַח pi.) ;] 
to cut in two, cut asunder: perh. metaphorically of severe scourging (but see Meyer on Mt, l.with, and cf. 1 Rois 15:33, 2 Rois 12:31, Hébreux 11:37), Matthieu 24:51, Luc 12:46.†

G1372.def:
διψάω,-ῶ
(δίψα, thirst), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא ;] 
to thirst: absol., Matthieu 25:35, 37 25:42, 44, Jean 4:13, 15 19:28, Romains 12:20" (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 4:11; figuratively, Jean 4:14 6:35 7:37, Apocalypse 7:16 21:6 22:17; with accusative (= cl. with genitive), τ. δικαιοσύνην, Matthieu 5:6.†

G1373.def:
δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό 
(late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for and cognates ;] 
thirst: 2 Corinthiens 11:27.†

G1374.def:
δίψυχος, -ον
(δίς, ψυχή), 
of two minds, wavering: Jacques 1:8 4:8 (Cremer, 588; DB, iv, 528).†

G1375.def:
διωγμός, -oῦ, ὁ
(διώκω), [in LXX: Proverbes 11:19 (רָדַף pi.), La 3:19 (מָרוּד), 2Ma.12:23 * ;] 
persecution: Matthieu 13:21, Marc 4:17 10:30 Actes 8:1 13:50, Romains 8:35, 2 Corinthiens 12:10, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:4, 2 Timothée 3:11.†

G1378.def:
δόγμα, -τος, τό
(δοκέω), [in LXX chiefly for דָּת, טְעֵם ;] 
__1. an opinion. 
__2. A public decree, ordinance: of Roman rulers, Luc 2:1, Actes 17:7; of the Jewish law, Éphésiens 2:15, Colossiens 2:14; of the Apostles, Actes 16:4 (Cremer, 205).†

G1379.def:
δογματίζω 
[in LXX: Esther 3:9 (כָּתַב ni.), Dan LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּת), I Esther 6:34, 2Ma.10:3 2Mac 15:36, 3Ma.4:11 * ;] 
to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Colossiens 2:20.†

G1380.def:
δοκέω, -ῶ
(δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב, etc. ;] 
__1. to be of opinion, suppose: Matthieu 24:44, Luc 12:40, Hébreux 10:29; with inf., Matthieu 3:9, Luc 8:18 24:37, Jean 5:39 16:2, Actes 12:9 27:13, 1 Corinthiens 3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37, Galates 6:3, Philippiens 3:4, Jacques 1:26; with accusative and inf., 1 Corinthiens 12:23, 2 Corinthiens 11:16; before ὅτι, Matthieu 6:7 26:53, Marc 6:49, Luc 12:51 13:2, 4 19:11, Jean 5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15, 1 Corinthiens 4:9, 2 Corinthiens 12:19, Jacques 4:5. 
__2. to seem, be reputed: Actes 25:27; with inf., Marc 10:42, Luc 10:36 22:24, Actes 17:13 26:9, 1 Corinthiens 11:16 12:22, 2 Corinthiens 10:9, Galates 2:6, 9, Hébreux 4:1 12:11; οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute, Galates 2:2. Impers., it seems, with dative of person(s); 
__(a) to think: Matthieu 17:25 18:12 21:28 22:17, 42 26:66, Jean 11:56, Hébreux 12:10; 
__(b) to please, seem good to: with inf., Luc 1:3, Actes 15:22, 25 15:23, 34.†
SYN. (δοκέω 1): ἡγέομαι 2, νομίζω2, οἴομαι; ἡ. and ν. properly express belief resting on external proof, ἡ. denoting the more careful judgment; δ. and οἴ. imply a subjective judgment which in the case of οἴ. is based on feeling, in δ. on thought (see Schmidt, with 17) (δοκέω2): φαίνομαι; φ., from the standpoint of the object, "expresses how a matter phenomenally shows and presents itself"; δ., from the standpoint of the observer, expresses one's subjective judgment about a matter (see Tr., Syn., LXXx; Cremer, 204).

G1381.def:
δοκιμάζω
(δόκιμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַן ;] 
__1. primarily of metals (Proverbes 8:10 17:3, Sir.2:5, Wis.3:6), to test, try, prove (in the hope and expectation that the test will prove successful, see reff. s. Syn.): χρυσίον, 1 Pierre 1:7; other things, Luc 12:56 14:19, 2 Corinthiens 8:8, Galates 6:4, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:4 5:21; τὰ διαφέροντα, Romains 2:18, Philippiens 1:10 (R, mg., but see infr.); πνεύματα, 1 Jean 4:1; of men, 1 Timothée 3:10 (pass.); ἑαυτόν, 1 Corinthiens 11:28, 2 Corinthiens 13:5; before subst. clause, Romains 12:2, 1 Corinthiens 3:13, Éphésiens 5:10 
__2. As the result of trial, to approve, think fit: Romains 1:28 14:22, 1 Corinthiens 16:3, 2 Corinthiens 8:22, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:4 (δεδοκιμάσμεθα); τὰ διαφέροντα, Romains 2:18, Philippiens 1:10, R, txt. (but see supr.; cf. διαφέρω).†

G1382.def:
δοκιμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(δόκιμος), [in Sm.: Psaumes 68:31 * ;] 
__1. the process of trial, proving, test: 2 Corinthiens 8:2 9:13 
__2. The result of trial, approval, approvedness, proof: Romains 5:4, 2 Corinthiens 2:9 13:3, Philippiens 2:22 (Cremer, 212, 701).†

G1383.def:
δοκίμιον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX: Proverbes 17:3 27:21 (מִצְרֵף) * ;] 
usually regarded as a variant form of δοκιμεῖον, a test, and so perh. Jacques 1:3 (see Mayor, in l), but see next word (cf. Cremer, 212, 702).†

G1384.def:
δοκίμιος, -α, -ον
(δοκιμή), [in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), Psaumes 12:6; and as seel. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זָקַק pual.), 1 Chroniques 29:4 (Bab); εἰ δ .ίστιν (יְקָר), Zacharie 11:13 א with a vid, Q *)* ;] 
= δόκιμος, 
tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, 1 Pierre 1:7 (where Hort suggests the seel. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), Jacques 1:3 (but see Mayor, in l For full discussion of this word, not hitherto found in a Gk. Lexicon, and for exx. of its use in π., see Deiss. (to whom is due the credit of its discovery), BS, 259 ff.; MM, Exp., xi; cf. also Milligan, NTD, 76).†
δόκιμος, -ον 
(δέκομαι = δέχομαι) [in LXX for זָקַק pual., etc. ;] 
primarily of metals, tested, accepted, approved: of persons, Romains 14:18 16:10, 1 Corinthiens 11:19, 2 Corinthiens 10:18 13:7, 2 Timothée 2:15, Jacques 1:12 (Cremer, 212, 697).†

G1385.def:
δοκός, -οῦ, ἡ
(δέχομαι) [in LXX for קוֹרָה, etc. ;] 
a beam of timber: Matthieu 7:3-5, Luc 6:41-42 (DCG, i, 176).†

G1386.def:
δόλιος, -α, -ον
(δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Sir—for etc. ;] 
deceitful: 2 Corinthiens 11:13.†

G1387.def:
δολιόω
(δόλιος), [in LXX: Nombres 25:18, Psaumes 105:25 (נָכַל), Psaumes 5:6 (חָלַק hi.) * ;] 
to deceive: ἐδολιοῦσαν (-σαν, frequently in κοινή Gk. for imperfect 3rd of person(s) pl.), Romains 3:13 (LXX).†

G1388.def:
δόλος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מִרְמָה;]
__1. in Hom., a bait. 
__2. a snare. 
__3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: Matthieu 26:4, Marc 7:22 14:1, Jean 1:47, Actes 13:10, Romains 1:29, 2 Corinthiens 12:16, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:3, 1 Pierre 2:1 2:22 3:10" (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).†

G1389.def:
δολόω, -ῶ
(δόλος) [in LXX: Psaumes 15:3 (רָגַל), Psaumes 36:2 (חָלַק hi.) * ;] 
__1. to ensnare. 
__2. As of wine, to adulterate, corrupt: τ. λόγον τ. θεοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 4:2.†
SYN.: καπηλεύω which see

G1390.def:
δόμα, -τος, τό
(δίδωμι), [in LXX for מַתָּנָה, etc. ;] 
a gift: Matthieu 7:11, Luc 11:13, Éphésiens 4:8" (LXX), Philippiens 4:17.†
SYN.: δόσις, δῶρον, δωρεά, δώρημα

G1391.def:
δόξα, -ης, ἡ 
(δοκέω), [in LXX very frequently for כָּבוֹד, also for הוֹד ,פִּפְאֶרֶת, etc., 25 words in all ;] 
in cl., 
__1. expectation, judgment, opinion (4Ma.5:18). 
__2. opinion, estimation in which one is held, repute; in NT, always good opinion, hence reputation, praise, honour, glory: Luc 14:10, Jean 12:43, Hébreux 3:3; opposite to αἰσχύνη, Philippiens 3:19; to ἀτιμία, 2 Corinthiens 6:8; δ. κ. τιμή, Romains 2:7, 10 1 Pierre 1:7, 2 Pierre 1:17; ζητεῖν, Jean 5:44 7:18 8:50, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:6; λαμβάνειν, Jean 5:41, 2 Pierre 1:17, Apocalypse 5:12; διδόναι δ. τ. θεῷ (cf. נָתַן כָּבוֹד לַיהוָֹה, Jérémie 13:16, al.), Luc 17:18, Jean 9:24, Actes 12:23, Romains 4:20, Apocalypse 4:9; εἰς (τ.) δ. θεοῦ, Romains 3:7 15:7, Philippiens 1:11, al.; in doxologies, τ. θεῷ (ᾧ) ἡ δ., Luc 2:14, Romains 11:36 16:27, Galates 1:5, Éphésiens 3:21, al. 
__3. Later also (not cl.) as in LXX (= הוֹד, Job 39:20, 1 Chroniques 29:25; כָּבוֹד, Job 19:9, Esther 5:11, al.), visible brightness, splendour, glory: of light, Actes 22:11; of heavenly bodies, 1 Corinthiens 15:40ff.; esp. that wh. radiates from God's presence, as manifested in the pillar of cloud and in the Holy of Holies (= כָּבוֹד, Exode 16:10 25:22 40:34, al.; and new Heb. שְׁכִינָה, 2Ma.2:8; see DB, iv, 489b), Romains 9:4, Jacques 2:1 (see Hort, Mayor, in l.); hence of the manifested glory of God, Romains 1:23, Colossiens 1:11 Éphésiens 1:6, 12 17 3:16; of the same as communicated to man through Christ, 2 Corinthiens 3:18 4:6; and of the glorious condition into which Christians shall enter hereafter, Romains 8:18, 21 9:23, 2 Timothée 2:10, al. 
SYN.: ἔπαινος τιμή (see Hort on 1 Pierre 1:7).

G1392.def:
δοξάζω
(δόξα), [in LXX chiefly for כָּבַד ni., pi., also for פָּאַר, etc. ;] 
__1. to think, suppose, hold an opinion (Æsch., Plat., al.). 
__2. To bestow δόξα (which see) on, to magnify, extol, praise (Thuc., iii, 45; Plut., al.): with accusative, Matthieu 5:16, Marc 2:12, Jean 8:54, Romains 15:6, 1 Pierre 2:12, al.; id. before ἐπί Luc 2:20; ἐν, Galates 1:24, 1 Pierre 4:16. 
__3. In LXX and NT (see: δόξα, 3), to clothe with splendour, glorify (Exode 34:29-30, Psaumes 37:20, Ésaïe 44:23, Esther 3:1, al): Romains 8:30, 2 Corinthiens 3:10, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:1, 1 Pierre 1:8, al.; of Christ, Jean 7:39 8:54, al. (on the Johannine use, see Cremer, 211; Westc., Jo., Intr.); of the Father, Jean 13:31-32, 1 Pierre 4:11, al. (cf. ἐν-, συν-δοξάζω).

G1393.def:
Δορκάς, -άδος, ἡ
(δορκάς, a gazelle), 
Dorcas, also called Ταβειθά, which see: Actes 9:36, 39.†

G1394.def:
δόσις, -εως, ἡ
(δίδωμι) [in LXX for חֹק (Genèse 47:22), (Proverbes 21:14 25:14), frequently in Sir. ;] 
__1. properly, the act of giving: Philippiens 4:15. 
__2. Objectively, a gift: Jacques 1:17.†
SYN.: see: δόμα

G1395.def:
δότης, -ου, ὁ
(δίδωμι), [in LXX: Proverbes 22:8 * ;] 
= δοτήρ, 
a giver: 2 Corinthiens 9:7 (LXX) (not elsewhere).†

G1396.def:
δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ
(δοῦλος, ἄγω), 
to make a slave, bring into bondage: 1 Corinthiens 9:27 (Cremer, 703).†

G1397.def:
δουλεία (T, -λία), -ας, ἡ 
(δουλεύω), [in LXX, as Exode 13:3, for עֶבֶד and cognates ;] 
slavery, bondage: Romains 8:15, 21 Galates 4:24 5:1, Hébreux 2:15.†

G1398.def:
δουλεύω
(δοῦλος), [in LXX for עָבַד, as Genèse 14:4, exc. Da TH Daniel 7:14, 27 (פְּלַח), Ésaïe 56:6 (שָׁרַת pi.)* ;] 
to be a slave, be subject to, serve: absol., Romains 7:6, Galates 4:25, 1 Timothée 6:2; with dative of person(s), Matthieu 6:24, Luc 15:29 16:13, Romains 9:12" (LXX) ; of nations, Jean 8:33, Actes 7:7" (LXX) ; θεῷ, τ. κυρίῳ, Matthieu 6:24, Luc 16:13, Actes 20:19, Romains 12:11 (R, mg., καιρῷ) Romains 16:18, Éphésiens 6:7, Colossiens 3:24, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:9; τ. Χριστῷ, Romains 14:18, Colossiens 3:24; νόμῳ θεοῦ, Romains 7:25; τ. θεοῖς, Galates 4:8; τ. καιρῷ, Romains 12:11 (R, mg. for κυρίῳ); ἀλλήλοις, Galates 5:13; σὺν ἐμοί Philippiens 2:22; τ. ἁμαρτίᾳ, Romains 6:6; νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας, Romains 7:25; 
ἐπιθυμίαις κ. ἡδοναις, Tite 3:3; τ. κοιλία, Romains 16:18; μαμωνᾷ, Matthieu 6:24, Luc 16:13; τ. στοιχείοις τ, κόσμου, Galates 4:9 (Cremer, 217).†
